answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. If an agent is caught duplicating identities to capture rewards, the protocol burns that stake, making a swarm of fake accounts costly rather than free. The stake is not proof of unique personhood, and a wealthy attacker can still buy influence; the defense raises the price of Sybil control. Reputation may grow along a trellis of verified work, while a ledge or meadow of empty accounts earns nothing.
